item.description:
Hold a key, speak, release. The text lands at your cursor. Nothing leaves the machine.
This one adds Underdog Bark, two English models that can leave out the ums for you, and gives every model its real name.
## Underdog Bark
Two English models from Conway Research, both retrained from Parakeet v3. They run on the Neural Engine and download about 440 MB each.
- **Bark Clean** writes what you meant to say. It leaves out "um" and "uh", false starts and repeated words as it transcribes. Pick it for dictation. - **Bark Verbatim** writes what you said, hesitations included. Pick it for meeting notes or anything that has to match the recording.
The first time you pick one, macOS prepares it for the Neural Engine, which takes one and a half to two and a half minutes. Anything you dictate meanwhile waits for it. After that it loads in seconds.
On a five-minute TED talk, Bark Clean was among the most accurate models utt offers, and both made fewer errors than Parakeet Standard. The numbers are on the blog: https://utt.jurrejan.com/blog/underdog-bark/
## Models go by their real names
Models made outside NVIDIA now carry the name their makers gave them: Parakeet Accurate is Parakeet Ultra again, Parakeet Compact is Parakeet Redux. NVIDIA's own models keep their names.
## Phonon-2 is gone
On an M2 Pro, Phonon-2 ran at half the speed of speech and took about twelve minutes to load every time utt started, because macOS rebuilt it for the Neural Engine on every load. If you had it selected, utt switches to Parakeet Standard.
## Extensions can run a dictation
An extension can now take over a dictation it starts with `utt://start?for=<id>`. utt shows no overlay and pastes nothing; it streams the level, the live words and the transcript to the extension, which draws them itself. The OpenCode plugin (`utt-opencode` on npm) uses this to dictate into OpenCode's prompt.
## Smaller things
- In the menu, Run unarmed (or Listen for the hotkey) now sits right under the status line, and Quit is on its own at the bottom. - utt is now MIT licensed.
